action_items: Fix AuthContext bootstrap so a stalled/timeout /api/auth/me on a protected route always transitions from user=null to guest/login after the bounded timeout in React StrictMode.

critical_code_review_comments: frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx sets didBootstrap.current=true before launching the async /auth/me loop. In React StrictMode, the first effect cleanup sets its local alive=false while the request is still pending; the second effect invocation returns early because didBootstrap is already true. When the stalled request times out/retries, the async branch cannot call setUser(false), leaving protected routes permanently at user=null/FullSpinner.

The auth bootstrap loop still retries /auth/me once on non-401 failures, so the stalled-auth test observed two /api/auth/me attempts. This conflicts with the stated 'fired ONCE on app load' expectation for the auth bootstrap.

rca_of_the_issue: Likely StrictMode bootstrap lifecycle bug: the didBootstrap useRef suppresses the second effect invocation, but the first invocation's cleanup marks alive=false before the delayed /auth/me promise settles. Therefore the timeout/retry path cannot update user state to false, so Protected keeps rendering the full-screen spinner. This preserves the user's reported '/api/auth/me pending/high load time leaves app stuck' symptom even though poller and Leads-list de-duping are now fixed. Test-only route delays/stubs were used to simulate slowness and positive poller widget data; product APIs are not mocked.
